bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Drafts Building Bye-Laws 2026 - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Drafts Building Bye-Laws 2026 16 Sep 2026 2 min read Why in News? The Bihar Government has prepared the draft Bihar Building Bye-Laws 2026 under its ongoing Deregulation 1.0 and 2.0 reforms . Key Points Self-Certification: The draft proposes self-certification for low-risk buildings to reduce lengthy approval procedures. Third-Party Inspection: Medium-risk buildings will undergo inspections by third parties under the proposed framework. A high-level review meeting on the reforms was jointly chaired by K.K. Pathak , Special Secretary, Cabinet Secretariat, Government of India, and Pratyaya Amrit , Chief Secretary, Bihar. Bihar EoDB Bill 2026: The Bihar Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) Bill 2026 received approval from the state legislature on July 23, 2026 , aiming to reduce regulatory hurdles for businesses and industries. The framework provides relief from dual licensing , while MSMEs can obtain approvals through self-declaration and receive protection from certain inspections. Digital Repository: Bihar launched a centralised digital repository for government rules, laws and orders on June 19, 2026 . More than 2,000 documents have been uploaded. The RTPS auto-appeal system was launched on June 23, 2026 , following Cabinet approval, to make public service delivery more accountable and efficient. Other Regulatory Reforms: The state has proposed or implemented measures including removing the requirement for Change of Land Use (CLU) in specified cases, speeding up electricity connections and removing minimum land requirements for private schools. Health Licensing: Bihar plans to develop an integrated health licensing portal to simplify licensing procedures in the healthcare sector. Tourism Reforms: Regulations have been simplified under the Mukhyamantri Homestay Protsahan Niti 2026 to promote homestays and tourism-related opportunities. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's Famous Vishnupad Temple To Get A ₹2520 Crore Makeover - Curly Tales
bihar_raw_news.content: Home / India / Trending / Bihar’s Famous Vishnupad Temple To Get A ₹2,520 Crore Makeover; Here’s What’s Planned For Pilgrims The Bihar government has now approved a ₹2,520 crore proposal to develop the premises and neighbouring areas of Vishnupad Temple in Gaya on the lines of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor. by Ashmeet Guliani Updated: September 16, 2026 3:22 PM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Wikimedia Commons/Keymaker31 The famous Vishnupad Temple, located in Gaya, Bihar, is all set to get a makeover. The government has approved a ₹2,520 crore proposal to develop the temple’s premises and its neighbouring areas. The temple is visited by thousands of people from all over the country to pray for their ancestors. Here’s everything you need to know about the development plan and the temple. Vishnupad Temple In Bihar Is Known For Lord Vishnu’s Footprint Dedicated to Lord Vishnu , Vishnupad Temple in Bihar features a 40 cm footprint that is believed to be Lord Vishnu’s. This is one of the reasons thousands of people from across and outside India visit this holy place. Not just that, it is also one of the most important places for a ritual called ‘Pinda Daan’. Many families perform this ritual to pray for their ancestors and seek peace for the souls of their departed family members. According to ETV Bharat, the Bihar government has now approved a ₹2,520 crore proposal to develop the premises and neighbouring areas of Vishnupad Temple in Gaya on the lines of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor. Plus, they will also spend ₹996 crore to link the Sone and Phalgu rivers. Also Read: 7th-Century Karpaga Vinayagar Temple Decked Up For Ganesh Chaturthi; Here’s What Makes It Special Development Plan To Improve Pilgrim Facilities The temple and its surroundings are located along the Phalgu River, which remains dry for the majority of the year. According to ETV Bharat, authorities believe that linking it with the Sone River could provide a regular water supply, even during the dry season. The development also focuses on providing better facilities to pilgrims while strengthening spiritual and religious tourism in Gaya. Reportedly, the development scheme will include work in the Vishnupad Temple precinct. This includes the development of the temple complex, multi-level car parking, elevated pathways and ghats along the banks of the Phalgu. Additionally, the project also includes the construction of statues, Sita Kund, public amenities and many other facilities in the temple premises. Vishnupad Temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. Why is Vishnupad Temple famous? The temple is famous for the footprint believed to be of Lord Vishnu and the Pinda Daan ritual. bihar_raw_news.title: Kashi model comes to Bihar : ₹2,520 crore makeover planned around Vishnupad Temple
bihar_raw_news.content: Kashi model comes to Bihar: ₹2,520 crore makeover planned around Vishnupad Temple Bihar has cleared a ₹2,520 crore Kashi-style makeover of Gaya Ji’s Vishnupad Temple area, with new ghats, pathways, parking and pilgrim facilities planned. Business Today Desk Updated Sep 16, 2026, 4:19 PM IST 1 / 5 Kashi blueprint Gaya Ji’s Vishnupad Temple is set for a sweeping makeover inspired by the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor in Varanasi. The Bihar Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, has approved ₹2,520 crore for the temple area, part of a larger ₹3,516.05 crore package. 2 / 5 Temple transformed The plan goes far beyond renovating Vishnupad Temple. It proposes multilevel parking, an elevated pathway, the Mansarwa Manpur Bridge, ramps, ghats, dormitories, a canteen, pedestrian bridge, statues, PFC Sita Kund and other public amenities, potentially reshaping how pilgrims experience Gaya Ji. 3 / 5 Ritual revival At the heart of the ₹2,520 crore makeover are traditions that have drawn pilgrims to Gaya Ji for generations. The government says the project is intended to strengthen infrastructure around rituals such as Pind Daan, Tarpan and Pitru Paksha, when the city sees large numbers of devotees. 4 / 5 River lifeline Alongside Vishnupad Temple, the Bihar Cabinet has cleared ₹996.05 crore for the Sone Phalgu River Linking Project. The plan includes an intake well about 23 km upstream of Indrapuri Barrage and an approximately 11 km pipeline to carry water towards the North Koel Main Canal. 5 / 5 ₹3,516 crore The scale of the Gaya Ji push is striking: ₹2,520 crore for the Vishnupad Temple area and ₹996.05 crore for the Sone Phalgu link. Together, the projects combine pilgrimage infrastructure, bridges, ghats, public facilities and water works in one major development package.

bihar_raw_news.content: September 16, 2026 Bihar Cabinet approves Vishnupad complex, river link Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service The Bihar Government on Tuesday approved Rs 3,516.05 crore for the Son-Falgu River Linking Project and to develop the Vishnupad Temple complex in Gayaji on the lines of the Kashi Vishwanath Corridor in Varanasi. It also accorded approval to a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to be signed between the Civil Aviation Ministry, the Airports Authority of India (AAI), and the state Government to expand air connectivity in the state under the Centre's Modified UDAN Scheme. According to the state tourism department's proposal that has been approved at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the estimated cost of the Vishnupad Temple complex development is Rs 2,520 crore, while the Son-Falgu River Linking Project is likely to cost Rs 996.05 crore. Under the Rs 2,520-crore Vishnupad Temple Complex development plan, the proposed works include development of the temple premises, construction and development of multilevel car parking, an elevated pathway, Manasarovar-Manpur Bridge, ramps, ghats, dormitory and canteen, pedestrian bridge, among others. The project will be implemented by Bihar Rajya Path Vikas Nigam Ltd (BRPNNL), said the tourism department's proposal. bihar_raw_news.title: ISMA Pegs India's Residential Rooftop Solar Potential at 132 GW - Saur Energy
bihar_raw_news.content: Solar News ISMA Pegs India’s Residential Rooftop Solar Potential at 132 GW The report identifies the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana as the primary catalyst behind the recent acceleration in residential rooftop solar deployment. Manish Kumar 16 Sep 2026 14:39 IST Follow Us ISMA Pegs India’s Residential Rooftop Solar Potential at 132 GW Photograph: (AI) India’s residential rooftop solar market has a potential of around 132 GW, with nearly 115 GW of capacity yet to be deployed, according to a new report by the Indian Solar Manufacturers Association (ISMA). Advertisment The report, titled “India’s Residential Rooftop Solar Market – Market Sizing & Growth Outlook”, estimates that residential rooftop solar capacity has reached around 17 GW. Overall, India’s grid-connected rooftop solar capacity stood at 30.11 GW as of June 30, 2026, with residential installations accounting for 16.66 GW, or 55.3% of the total. Advertisment PM Surya Ghar-A Catalyst The report identifies the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana as the primary catalyst behind the recent acceleration in residential rooftop solar deployment. The scheme, launched in February 2024, had contributed around 13.45 GW of rooftop solar capacity by July 2026, according to the report. As of August 2026, around 77.85 lakh households had registered under the scheme, while 14,953 MW of installations had been completed, equivalent to around half of the FY27 target of one crore households. Gujarat led the states with 2,924 MW of installed capacity under the scheme, followed by Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Kerala and Rajasthan. Together, the five states accounted for around 69% of the capacity installed under PM Surya Ghar. Advertisment ISMA estimates that the residential rooftop market could support annual installations of 9-15 GW between 2026 and 2030. The association said this could create a sustained demand pipeline for solar cells, modules, inverters and balance-of-system components. 132GW Estimate The report's 132 GW estimate is based on a bottom-up assessment of residential electricity consumption rather than simply available rooftop area. ISMA starts with India's residential electricity consumption of 375 BU and a representative solar yield of 1,250 kWh/kW/year, resulting in a consumption-based ceiling of around 300 GW. Advertisment This is then adjusted for home ownership, solid-roof structures, flats and system sizing. Under the central scenario, ISMA arrives at 132.3 GW of residential rooftop potential. Its sensitivity analysis puts the potential at 111.1 GW under the conservative scenario and 153.4 GW under the aggressive scenario. Advertisment However, the report estimates that only around 8 GW of the residential market can currently support rooftop solar without subsidy. ISMA assessed 14 states covering roughly three-fourths of national residential electricity demand and applied an eight-year payback threshold. Five States Dominate Five states — Maharashtra, Kerala, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Assam — crossed the threshold. Together, they account for around 23% of national residential electricity demand. ISMA estimates that the resulting subsidy-independent market, after accounting for high-consumption households, is approximately 8 GW. bihar_raw_news.title: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan to visit Bihar on September 16 to review flood situation
bihar_raw_news.content: ANI Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will visit Bihar on September 16 to inspect flood-affected areas, visit relief camps, and evaluate emergency operations. New Delhi: Union Minister for Agriculture Shivraj Singh Chouhan will visit Bihar on Wednesday, September 16, to assess the overall flood situation and evaluate the related damage across the state. During the visit, the Union Minister will conduct an extensive aerial survey of various flood-affected areas of the state, interact directly with affected farmers and common people, and review relief and rescue operations in a high-level meeting with senior officials in the presence of Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary . A team of senior officials from the Union Ministries of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development will also accompany Shivraj Singh during the tour. Read more: Shivraj Singh Chouhan seeks faster credit for women, meets banks As per the scheduled programme, Chouhan will reach Patna from Bhopal and conduct an aerial survey of the flood-affected areas of Dighwara and Maner by helicopter from Patna State Hangar at 10:30 AM. Live Events Following his arrival at the Hajipur Police Line at 11:00 AM, he will travel by road to Tersia and Saraipur villages. There, he will inspect the damage caused to crops by the floods and interact directly with local farmers. After taking stock of the flood-affected areas, Shivraj Singh Chouhan will visit 'Samvad', Chief Minister's Secretariat, at 12:15 PM. Read more: Chouhan urges states to speed up watershed projects He will also participate in an important review meeting on flood disaster management , relief works and assistance to be provided to farmers, with Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and senior officials. Departing from Patna at 1:30 PM, Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan will visit Nawabgarhi in Munger at around 2:15 PM. At Nawabgarhi, he will visit the relief camp and will meet flood victims and assess the quality of ongoing relief work. After this, he will travel by road via Bhagalpur to inspect the Kosi-Karaiya embankment in Navgachia. In the evening, he will visit the relief camp at Bhagalpur Polytechnic College to meet the affected families taking shelter there and enquire about their well-being. Shivraj Singh will also meet flood-affected people on the morning of September 17 before leaving for Patna. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! bihar_raw_news.content: English News National Lakhimpur Houses Swept Away | Bihar Floods & Punjab Rain Alert 50 lakh people affected in flood hit Bihar: 7 houses swept away in UP's Lakhimpur, landslide in Uttarakhand's Pithoragarh New Delhi 14 hours ago Copy link In Bihar, around 50 lakh people across 575 panchayats in 15 districts remain surrounded by floodwater. In Katihar, government schools and coaching centres have been submerged, with children now attending classes seated in boats. A yellow alert for rain has been issued for 26 districts of the state, along with a warning for lightning strikes. In UP, rivers are in spate due to rain, with flood conditions in 26 districts affecting nearly 4 lakh people. In Lakhimpur, accelerated erosion by the Sharda river has swept away 7 houses in the past 24 hours. In Uttarakhand's Pithoragarh, the road on the Adi Kailash route at Dobat has been shut again due to a landslide. In Rudraprayag, pilgrims are being sent along the Kedarnath trekking route near Cheerbasa wearing helmets as a safety measure. Several horses and mules were killed in a landslide there four days ago, and complaints of foul smell and breathing difficulties have emerged due to carcasses lying along the route. In Rajasthan, a yellow alert for rain has been issued for 26 districts until 17 September. Light to moderate rain fell in Ajmer, Pali and some other districts on Tuesday. Meanwhile, in Madhya Pradesh, rain is expected in the western region from 17-19 September and in the eastern region from 18-21 September. bihar_raw_news.content: Breaking A ☀ ☽ Supreme Court pulls up states over menstrual hygiene compliance, flags gaps in Jharkhand and Bihar THE JHARKHAND STORY NETWORK New Delhi, September 16: The Supreme Court has expressed dissatisfaction with the manner in which States and Union… September 16, 2026 · 5 min read Share WhatsApp X Facebook Copy link THE JHARKHAND STORY NETWORK New Delhi, September 16: The Supreme Court has expressed dissatisfaction with the manner in which States and Union Territories have reported compliance with its directions on menstrual hygiene facilities in schools, observing that some responses appeared to be mere formalities and did not accurately reflect the situation on the ground. A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice R Mahadevan, while monitoring compliance with its judgment in Jaya Thakur v. Government of India & Ors. , 2026, examined the affidavit filed by the Union of India and observed that although substantial progress had been made, much more needed to be done to make the right to menstrual health meaningful. The Court’s observations are significant for Jharkhand and Bihar, which were among the States where discrepancies were found in data relating to menstrual waste-disposal systems. Stay informed. Get Jharkhand's top stories in your inbox. Free. No spam. Unsubscribe anytime. Supreme Court questions compliance reports The Supreme Court had earlier directed pan-India implementation of the Union government’s Menstrual Hygiene Policy for School-going Girls in schools for adolescent girls studying in Classes 6 to 12. The directions require all government and private schools in urban and rural areas to provide functional gender-segregated toilets with usable water connectivity, accessible and private toilet facilities, functional washing facilities with soap and water, free sanitary napkins and menstrual hygiene management (MHM) corners. Advertisement During the latest hearing on September 1, 2026, the bench examined reports submitted by the States, Union Territories and the Union government regarding further compliance with its directions. According to the Union government’s affidavit, of the 39,439 girls’ toilets identified as remaining to be made functional, 30,458 had been constructed, 4,236 were under construction, and 4,745 remained as a gap. The Union also reported an expansion of handwashing facilities, sanitary napkin distribution, MHM corners, vending machines and waste-disposal mechanisms. Several States and UTs were reported to have achieved complete or near-complete coverage of various facilities. Advertisement However, the Court said that merely submitting numerical figures was insufficient. “We are discontent with the manner in which compliance is reported. The response by some States exhibit non-application of mind or rather mere formality,” the Court observed, noting that some States had indicated compliance through statistics or simple yes/no responses even where a more detailed response was required. Discrepancies found in State data The Court pointed to several inconsistencies in the compliance data submitted by States. Several States claimed saturation of toilet facilities even though the number of toilets accessible to children with special needs was lower than the total number of schools. bihar_raw_news.title: SJVN commissions Unit-II of Buxar Thermal Power Project
bihar_raw_news.content: SJVN Limited, through its wholly owned subsidiary SJVN Thermal Private Limited, has achieved commercial operation of the 660 MW Unit-II of its 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project in Bihar. Located at Chausa in Buxar district, the project comprises two 660 MW units and uses supercritical technology. It has been developed at a total investment of approximately Rs 137.57 billion, revised at the June 2025 price level. The project is expected to generate 9,828.72 million units of electricity annually, of which 85 per cent has been allocated to Bihar under a long-term power purchase agreement. Unit-I of the project had already achieved commercial operation on November 14, 2025. With the commissioning of Unit-II, the entire 1,320 MW capacity has been brough into commercial operation. The project is expected to improve power availability in Bihar and the eastern region, reduce peak-hour shortages and strengthen energy security. It is also SJVN’s first thermal power project to become fully operational.

national_raw_news.title: 34 mins ago | Regional News 26 India Electric Mobility Index 2025 announced by NITI Aayog; Delhi emerges top performer in adopti...
national_raw_news.content: Delhi has been ranked top performer in States and UT in Electric Mobility adoption as per the India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI) 2025. The Index was launched by the NITI Aayog in New Delhi today, which outlines both the policy framework and implementation outcomes for e-mobility at the sub-national level. After Delhi, the other top-performing States and UTs are Maharashtra, Karnataka, Chandigarh and Goa. This is the second edition of the Index and it measures the progress of States and Union Territories in achieving their Electric Mobility goals. Speaking at the release of the index, NITI Aayog Member Rajiv Guaba said that the transition to electric mobility is an economic, environmental and strategic imperative to the ambition of Viksit Bharat by 2047. Mr Guaba highlighted that there is a shift towards electric mobility, and by 2040, it is estimated that 40 percent of all new car sales would be electric. He noted that India has built one of the most aggressive, targeted e-mobility frameworks in the world. The Member said that the top score of States and Union Territories has improved from 77 in 2024 to 84 in 2025. The IEMI tracks, evaluates and scores all Indian States and UTs out of 100 across 16 indicators under three core themes, Transport Electrification Progress, Charging Infrastructure Readiness and EV Research and Innovation Status. It aims to inform decision-making, foster healthy competition among states, and promote sharing of best practices.

national_raw_news.title: Cabinet raises EPFO mandatory coverage wage ceiling to Rs 25,000; 51 lakh more workers ...
national_raw_news.content: Cabinet raises EPFO mandatory coverage wage ceiling to Rs 25,000; 51 lakh more workers to benefit Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Cabinet raises EPFO mandatory coverage wage ceiling to Rs 25,000; 51 lakh more workers to benefit ANI | Updated: Sep 16, 2026 15:31 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 16 (ANI): The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved an increase in the wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) to Rs 25,000 per month from Rs 15,000, a move expected to bring more than 51 lakh additional employees under mandatory social security coverage. The decision was announced by Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw during a briefing following the Cabinet meeting. According to a release issued by the govt, the proposal to raise the wage ceiling by Ministry of Labour and Employment was approved by the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. At present, a fresh employee joining employment with wages above Rs 15,000 per month is not automatically covered under the EPF framework and may remain outside mandatory provident fund, pension and associated insurance protection. With the ceiling now raised to Rs 25,000, employees falling in the Rs 15,000-Rs 25,000 monthly wage band will come within the statutory social security framework. The move will expand access to provident fund savings, pension protection under the Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and insurance protection under the Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI), subject to applicable scheme provisions. The EPFO wage ceiling was last revised in September 2014, when it was increased to Rs 15,000. Prior to that, the ceiling had remained unchanged between 2004 and 2014. The government said the latest revision reflects sustained wage growth, rising incomes and the expansion of formal employment over the intervening period. The annual government outgo following the enhancement is estimated at about Rs 11,339 crore, compared with the existing annual budgetary support of around Rs 10,250 crore. The estimated expenditure over five years is about Rs 56,696 crore. The government expects the measure to support further formalisation of employment, improve long-term retirement security and widen access to portable statutory social security benefits. EPFO currently administers the Employees’ Provident Fund, Employees’ Pension Scheme and Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme. According to the latest EPFO data cited by the government, the organisation has around 7.98 crore contributing members across about 7.68 lakh contributing establishments, while the EPS provides pension benefits to around 82 lakh pensioners. The Ministry of Labour and Employment and EPFO will now undertake the necessary statutory and administrative steps to implement the Cabinet decision. national_raw_news.content: Europe's Missile Manufacturing Revolution: Affordable Arsenal for Modern Warfare | International About Career Advertisement Media Partnership Contact Us HOME NEWS RESEARCH LIVE DISCOURSE PERSPECTIVES AND INSIGHTS SUBMIT PRESS RELEASE NEWS DESK RESEARCH LIVE DISCOURSE PERSPECTIVES AND INSIGHTS INTERVIEW Home News Article Europe's Missile Manufacturing Revolution: Affordable Arsenal for Modern Warfare European militaries are shifting toward producing cheaper missiles and interceptors after conflicts revealed the limits of small inventories. This demand comes amid ongoing conflicts, exemplified by Ukraine's response to Russia's attacks. Emerging startups seek to meet this need while major industry players focus on scaling production capacity. Devdiscourse News Desk | Updated: 16-09-2026 11:30 IST | Created: 16-09-2026 11:30 IST India's nuclear capable missiles of Agni series (Photo/ PIB) SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... European armies are increasingly turning to cost-effective missile production in light of recent conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East which exposed the challenges of maintaining high-end weapon inventories. On the eastern front, Russia's relentless drone and missile strikes on Ukraine have underscored that modern warfare depletes weapon supplies faster than anticipated, a fact often overlooked in peacetime planning. Douglas Barrie from the International Institute for Strategic Studies highlighted the precariousness of relying solely on high-end weapons. As Europe's defense industry shifts focus to scalable production of low-cost systems, startups and established firms like Lockheed Martin and MBDA aim to meet the growing demands alongside enhancing existing capacities. The ongoing transformation marks a strategic pivot towards efficient, large-scale manufacturing in modern warfare. (With inputs from agencies.) national_raw_news.title: COAS General Seth embarks on three-day Russia visit to strengthen defence ties
national_raw_news.content: COAS General Seth embarks on three-day Russia visit to strengthen defence ties Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर COAS General Seth embarks on three-day Russia visit to strengthen defence ties ANI | Updated: Sep 16, 2026 11:32 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 16 (ANI): Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth began an official three-day visit to Russia on Wednesday aimed at further strengthening the longstanding India- Russia defence partnership and military-to-military cooperation. According to an official release issued by the Ministry of Defence, General Seth is visiting Russia from September 16 to September 18. During the visit, the Army Chief will receive a ceremonial Guard of Honour and pay tribute to fallen soldiers at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Moscow. He will also hold discussions with Colonel General Andrei Nikolayevich Mordvichev, Commander-in-Chief of the Russia n Land Forces, on issues of mutual interest, including professional military cooperation and training. The visit comes against the backdrop of longstanding military-technical cooperation between India and Russia , which has evolved from a buyer-seller relationship towards joint research, development and production of advanced defence technologies and systems. In Moscow, General Seth is scheduled to visit the National Defence Control Centre and interact with senior officials of the Russia n Ministry of Defence, including Deputy Defence Minister Vasily Sergeyevich Osmakov, who handles defence industry and procurement. The engagements will provide an opportunity for both sides to exchange perspectives on contemporary military developments and explore avenues for enhancing defence cooperation, according to the release. The Army Chief will also travel to Saint Petersburg, where he is scheduled to visit the Mikhailovskaya Military Artillery Academy and interact with its leadership and faculty. The Ministry of Defence said the visit "reflects the importance attached by both countries to sustained military diplomacy and Army-to-Army engagement". The interactions are expected to further deepen military cooperation and reinforce the enduring defence relationship between India and Russia . Russia remains an important source for India's defence equipment, engines, spare parts and components. According to the Ministyr of External Affairs, several Russia n-origin platforms are also assembled or produced in India, including T-90 tanks and Su-30 MKI aircraft. The two countries have also been exploring co-development and co-production of defence equipment and platforms, including the possibility of exports to other countries involving the BrahMos system. The India- Russia defence relationship has also included naval cooperation. INS Tamal, described as the latest stealth multi-role frigate, was commissioned in Kaliningrad on July 1, 2025. national_raw_news.content: Rs 10,998 Crore Varuna Elevated Corridor To Link NH-31 With Varanasi Ring Road, Cut Airport And Kashi Station Travel Time Infrastructure Rs 10,998 Crore Varuna Elevated Corridor To Link NH-31 With Varanasi Ring Road, Cut Airport And Kashi Station Travel Time Swarajya Staff Sep 16, 2026 | Updated 10:12 AM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Map of the proposed Varun Corridor in Varanasi (Pic Via PIB) The Rs 10,998-crore Varuna Elevated Corridor in Varanasi is set to create a new high-capacity road link between NH-31 and the Varanasi Ring Road, with the project aimed at easing pressure on congested urban routes while improving access to the airport, railway stations and major commercial and pilgrimage destinations. The 43.218-km corridor, approved by the Union Cabinet in July, will run along the Varuna River and form an important component of Varanasi’s future transport network. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, will develop the predominantly elevated 6/4-lane corridor. The project will include the main carriageway, flyovers, loops, ramps and service roads, along with an iconic cable-stayed bridge and an extradosed foot over bridge-cum-major bridge. Part Of Varanasi’s Wider Decongestion Plan The project forms part of the Varanasi Decongestion Plan and is designed to improve movement between the city’s major highways, railway stations, airport and other important urban destinations. The direct connection between NH-31 and the Varanasi Ring Road is expected to improve access to Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport as well as Varanasi Cantonment, Varanasi City Railway Station, Kashi Railway Station and Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction. The corridor will also strengthen connectivity to Ramnagar Port and areas located along the Varuna corridor. Designed for operating speeds of 80-100 kmph, the corridor is expected to halve travel time between NH-31 and Kashi Railway Station from around 40 minutes to nearly 20 minutes. According to the road transport ministry, the shorter journey is expected to improve traffic flow, reduce vehicle operating costs and enable more efficient passenger and freight movement. Airport Journey Could Fall To Around 20 Minutes One of the most significant projected benefits involves connectivity between Varanasi Junction and Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport. The journey currently takes nearly an hour, according to the government release , but is projected to fall to around 20 minutes once the corridor becomes operational. The new infrastructure is also expected to ease traffic pressure around major congestion points including Varanasi Junction, Phulwaria and Chaukaghat, where local, commercial and through traffic currently compete for limited road capacity. The elevated alignment, together with planned ramps, loops and service roads, is intended to create a dedicated route for regional and through traffic and separate longer-distance traffic from local movement. Global chipmakers, policymakers and investors will fill the halls behind him, all watching an industry India has built from the ground up. For three days, the country's semi-con (semiconductor) manufacturing story will be on full display. For an industry that barely had a heartbeat in India a decade ago, this is not just a conference. It is the moment India’s semiconductor ambitions step into the spotlight. The theme this year is " Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem ." That phrase carries more weight than it first appears to. India is no longer asking whether it can make chips. It is now asking how fast it can build everything around them. The Object That Runs the World Hold up your phone. Somewhere inside it sits a piece of silicon smaller than a postage stamp, carrying billions of transistors switching on and off, billions of times a second. Apple's A19 Bionic chip, built at 3 nanometres, packs roughly 30 billion transistors onto that tiny surface. It is, without exaggeration, one of the most complex objects human beings have ever built. Chips are not a niche product anymore. They sit inside cars, drones, aeroplanes, MRI machines and satellites. At the moment, the global electronics industry is valued at around $4.3 trillion and growing fast. Semiconductors sit right at the base of this growing structure, forming it’s foundation. Every other industry, from automobiles to healthcare to defence, depends on what comes out of a chip fabrication plant. That is what makes semiconductors a foundational industry. Miss this layer, and every layer above it becomes fragile. The world learned this the hard way. For example, during the COVID pandemic, car factories faced shutdowns. Not because of a lack of steel or labour, but because they could not get chips. Countries that had spent decades treating semiconductors as someone else's problem suddenly scrambled to build their own capacity. The pandemic did not create the race for chips. It simply forced everyone to run faster. A Long Road to This Moment India's interest in semiconductors goes back further than most people realise, decades of quiet attempts, small starts, and lessons learned the hard way. For a long time, the ambition was there, but the ecosystem around it never quite came together. That changed with a different approach. Reforms in foreign investment, taxation and customs opened the door wide. Global electronics companies slowly began setting up manufacturing lines in India, and the results are hard to argue with.
